chunks: My father, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Hariz, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

There is no one who possesses wealth of gold or silver who withholds its zakat, except that Allah, Exalted and Glorious, will constrain him on the Day of Resurrection in a place called Qarqar, and set upon him a bald snake that seeks to seize him while he moves away from it. When he sees that he cannot rid himself of it, it will allow him to grasp its hand and gnaw it like a radish is gnawed, and then it will become a collar on his neck.
And the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious: 'They will be encircled with that which they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection.'

And there is no one who possesses property of camels, cows, or sheep who withholds its zakat, except that Allah, Exalted and Glorious, will constrain him on the Day of Resurrection in a place called Qarqar, where every creature with a hoof will trample him with its hoof, and every creature with a canine tooth will snap at him with its tooth.

And there is no one who possesses property of palm trees, grapes, or crops who withholds its zakat, except that Allah will encircle his neck with the noose of his land until seven lands until the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for withholding zakat on gold, silver, and livestock according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to elucidate the specific eschatological punishments for neglecting zakat, categorizing retribution by wealth type: gold and silver are bound by a 'bald snake' (shuja'a aqra'), livestock owners are trampled by their own animals, and agriculturalists face chains extending to the seventh earth. This hadith provides the exegetical basis for the term 'Qarqar' as a place of confinement and illustrates the physical manifestation of stinginess as a divine constraint, reinforcing the spiritual danger of hoarding wealth.
